_about: Machine-readable merge tiers for Project 2050. Read by .github/scripts/agent_gate.py. The plain-language rules are in charter/STANDARDS.md (merge categories) and legacy/governing/project-collaboration.md (gate details); changing this file is itself a tier 3 change. Patterns use fnmatch syntax against repository paths; the first matching rule wins.
_trusted_note: Only comments and labels from these accounts count. Today every agent posts as Espen's account; add machine-account logins here if they are created. Anyone can comment on a public repository, so this list is what stops outsiders from approving.
_agents_note: apps: the GitHub App slug GitHub records (performed_via_github_app) when that agent comments or labels through its integration. Observed Oct 26 in the gate log: Claude Code 'claude' (PR #27), Codex 'chatgpt-codex-connector' (PR #26 review). A review must come through its own agent's app when one is listed, and never through another agent's app. independent_sessions false: that vendor's sessions cannot review each other's PRs (Codex runs as one recurring hourly task, so a later run reviewing an earlier run's work is self-review).

rules.why: the merge rules and checks themselves
charter: plan, standards, outcomes and decisions
dossier drafts; design choices at real forks go to Espen as decision memos
model code, cards and data; outputs they change are classified separately
the preserved tree is read-only; the model suite's generated outputs are classified separately

_generated_note: legacy/index/check-report.md lists document findings; it changes whenever a checked document does, so on its own it counts as a wording-level output (tier 1), not a model change.

headlines._about: Tests and the 2040 margin: any change is tier 3. Other headline numbers: tier 2 if every relative change is within tolerance, tier 3 otherwise.
